paragraphs: Portillo's Inc. (the "Company") was incorporated as a Delaware corporation on June 8, 2021, for the purpose of facilitating an initial public offering ("IPO") and other related transactions in order to carry on the business of PHD Group Holdings LLC and its subsidiaries ("Portillo's OpCo"). The Company became the sole managing member of Portillo's OpCo and operates and controls all of the business and affairs of Portillo's OpCo. As a result, the Company consolidates the financial results of Portillo's OpCo and reports a non-controlling interest representing the economic interest in Portillo's OpCo held by the other members of Portillo's OpCo (the "pre-IPO LLC Members"). Portillo's Inc. Class A common stock trades on the Nasdaq under the symbol "PTLO." Unless the context otherwise requires, references to "we," "us," "our," "Portillo's," the "Company" and other similar references refer to Portillo's Inc. and its subsidiaries, including Portillo's OpCo.

As of the fiscal year ended December 28, 2025 ("fiscal 2025"), we owned and operated 102 restaurants across 11 states, including a restaurant owned by C&O Chicago, L.L.C. ("C&O") of which we own 50% of the equity. As of December 28, 2025, the Company owned 95.4% of Portillo's OpCo and the pre-IPO LLC Members owned the remaining 4.6% of Portillo's OpCo.
The Company entered into a joint venture agreement to develop and operate a restaurant at the Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport ("DFW")
which is expected to commence operations in 2026. The Company holds a 65% ownership interest in AP Dogs, LLC ("AP Dogs") and has day-to-
day operational and managerial control over its business and affairs. Accordingly, the Company consolidates the joint venture and reports a
noncontrolling interest representing the economic interest in AP Dogs held by the other partner.

Portillo's serves iconic Chicago street food in high-energy, multichannel restaurants designed to ignite the senses and create memorable dining experiences. Since our founding in 1963 in a small trailer that Dick Portillo called "The Dog House," we have grown to become a treasured brand with a passionate (some might say obsessed) nationwide following. Our diverse menu features all-American favorites such as Chicago-style hot dogs and sausages, Italian beef sandwiches, char-broiled burgers, fresh chopped salads, crinkle-cut fries, homemade chocolate cake and our signature chocolate cake shake. We create a consumer experience like no other by combining the best attributes of fast-casual and quick-service ("QSR") concepts with an exciting energy-filled atmosphere in a restaurant model capable of generating tremendous volumes. Nearly all of our restaurants were built with double lane drive-thrus and have been thoughtfully designed with a layout that accommodates a variety of access modes including dine-in, carryout, delivery and catering to quickly and efficiently serve our guests. We believe the combination of our craveable food, multichannel sales model, dedication to operational excellence, and distinctive team member-driven culture gives us a competitive advantage. Our business, including many of the elements described below, is subject to certain risks that may materially and adversely affect our ability to achieve our desired outcomes. For a more in-depth discussion of such risks, see Part I, Item 1A, "Risk Factors."

An Iconic and Beloved Brand with Obsessed, Lifelong Fans. We capture the hearts, minds and stomachs of our guests with every meal served. Our menu features something for everyone and appeals to a broad demographic, which enables our restaurants to thrive and generate strong and balanced volumes across multiple dayparts, weekdays and occasions.

Energetic Restaurant Atmosphere that Engages the Senses. While our operating model is focused on getting delicious, made-to-order food to our guests quickly, we believe our atmosphere makes the experience more than a delicious meal. When guests walk into a Portillo's, they are immersed in an experience unlike any chain restaurant visit. Our restaurants engage all the senses to create a fun, relaxed and memorable occasion.

Our dining areas evoke nostalgia and local influences. Each of our restaurants has its own themed décor, ranging from a 1930s prohibition motif to a 1950s diner to a 1960s flower-power bus, as well as a retro automotive garage theme. The music ties to the theme, from ragtime to doo wop to disco. No detail is too small, be it lighting, signage or even the stars subtly sparkling on the ceiling. Each restaurant also draws design elements from the local community. The layouts create comfortable spaces for individual diners, families, large groups, and even wedding parties.

Beyond the space itself, we believe the energy of Portillo's is unique. Our guests can see into our open kitchens, where their meals are prepared right before their eyes. The smells of burgers broiling, french fries frying, and beef simmering in gravy emanate from the kitchen. Each completed meal is announced with a fun rhyme ("Number two, we got you!"; "Number seven, welcome to Portillo's heaven!"). But the most important element of the energy is the enthusiasm of the scores of guests who are all excited to be there and enjoying their Portillo's experience. We want every guest that visits to leave with good memories, a satiated appetite and a desire to return.

Maintaining the Fabric of our Beloved Brand. Portillo's aims to offer industry-leading experiences across our traditional sales channels, while continuing to grow and innovate in growth sales channels. Dine-in provides the best Portillo's experience, so we strive for our dine-in experience to represent the heart of Portillo's and our values of Family, Greatness, Energy, and Fun. In our drive-thru, we strive to maintain top performance in the industry across speed, service, and accuracy. In our sales channels of digital pickup, delivery, and catering we have made great strides operationally that will allow us to win additional market share.

Portillo's pioneered our drive-thru model beginning in the 1980s, combining speed and hospitality via outside order takers, food runners, and multi-lane drive-thrus. Our teams are focused on continuously improving and innovating the drive-thru experience to improve throughput and order accuracy. New restaurants are opened with drive-thru doors to aid our runners and improve the guest experience.

Experience, service, and food quality define value in our brand, but maintaining a strong price point remains a high priority given how broadly we compete in the restaurant industry. We consistently monitor price points across many categories and occasions that are relevant to our guests. To succeed moving forward, we will continue our pricing strategy combined with a focus on operational excellence and aim to remain an unrivaled value compared to fast-casual competitors.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business, Industry and Growth Strategies
We are vulnerable to changes in economic conditions, increases in food and commodity costs and consumer preferences.
We may fail to open new restaurants or establish new markets or our new restaurants may not perform as well as anticipated, may not be profitable, or may close.
Our growth plans and ongoing capital expenditure ("capex") needs require us to spend capital, which may not be readily available.
Our same-restaurant sales may be lower than we expect in future periods.
Food safety concerns and incidents involving food-borne illness could have an adverse effect on our business.

We face significant competition for guests, and our inability to compete effectively may affect our traffic, our sales and our operating profit margins, which could have a material adverse effect on our Results.
Our restaurant base is geographically concentrated in the Midwestern United States, and we could be negatively affected by conditions specific to that region.
Damage to our reputation and negative publicity could have a material adverse effect on our Results.
The digital and delivery business, and expansion thereof, is uncertain and subject to inherent risk.
Any prolonged disruption in the operations of our two commissaries could harm our business.
Failure to maintain our corporate culture as we grow could have a material adverse effect on our business.
Matters relating to employment and labor law could have a material adverse effect, result in litigation or union activities, add significant costs and divert management attention.
Labor quality, labor shortages or increased labor costs could have a material adverse effect on our Results.
We are exposed to risks associated with leasing property including long-term, non-cancelable leases and potential inability to renew expiring leases.
Our business is subject to risks related to our sale of alcoholic beverages.
An impairment in the carrying value of our goodwill, indefinite-lived intangible assets or long-lived assets could have a material adverse effect on our business.

Natural disasters, unusual weather conditions, pandemic outbreaks, political events, war and terrorism could disrupt our business and result in lower sales, increased operating costs and capital expenditures.
The focus on environmental sustainability and social initiatives could increase our costs, harm our reputation, and adversely impact our Results.

Our inability or failure to execute on a comprehensive business continuity plan at our Restaurant Support Center following a disaster or force majeure event could have a material adverse impact on our Results.
Our level of indebtedness could have a material adverse effect on our business and limit our ability to plan for or respond to changes in our business.
Risks Related to Our Organizational Structure
In certain circumstances, Portillo's OpCo will be required to make distributions to us and the other holders of LLC Units, and those distributions may be substantial.
Our organizational structure, including the Tax Receivable Agreement ("TRA"), introduces complexity into our business.
Risks Related to Intellectual Property, Information Technology, and Data Security
The failure to protect and maintain our intellectual property, including our trademarks, could have a material adverse effect on our business.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider each of the following risk factors in conjunction with other information provided in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and in our other public disclosures. Our business is subject to a number of risks, including risks that may prevent us from achieving our business objectives or may adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, liquidity or access to sources of financing, and/or the market value of our Class A common stock. These risks could cause our future results to differ materially from historical results and from guidance we may provide regarding our expectations of future financial performance. The risks described below highlight potential events, trends or other circumstances that could adversely affect our business.

Like other companies in the restaurant industry, we are dependent upon food and commodity availability and their costs impact our business and results. Food and commodity costs and availability can be volatile and are affected by factors outside of our control, including general economic conditions, inflation, labor shortages, seasonal fluctuations, weather and climate conditions, energy costs, global demand, trade protections and subsidies, food safety issues, infectious diseases, possible terrorist activity, cyberattacks, transportation issues, currency fluctuations, product recalls, and government regulations, among others.

Food and commodity cost volatility has affected our profitability and reputation in the past and could do so in the future. While a portion of our commodities are subject to contract pricing, as our contracts expire we may unable to successfully (re)negotiate terms that protect us from inflation or the portion not covered by contract pricing might increase unexpectedly, creating unplanned price inflation. We experienced 3.9% and 4.2% commodity price inflation for the years ended December 28, 2025 and December 29, 2024, respectively.

If the cost of our ingredients increase, we may suspend or permanently discontinue certain menu items rather than pay the increased cost for the ingredients. These changes to our menu could negatively impact our restaurant traffic and operational results during the shortage and thereafter. Additionally, we may be unable to offset all or even a portion of a future cost increase through menu price increases. Competitive conditions may limit our menu pricing flexibility and implementing menu price increases may change our guests' visit frequencies or purchasing patterns. Our industry depends on consumer discretionary spending and is affected by changes in consumer tastes, and macro- and micro-economic conditions (including economic downturns, consumer sentiment, inflation or increased food or energy costs). Factors such as traffic patterns, weather, fuel prices, local demographics, local regulations and the competitive landscape may adversely affect the performances of our individual locations.

Our restaurants are primarily located in high-activity trade areas that often contain retail, lifestyle, and entertainment centers. We depend on high visitor rates in these trade areas to attract guests to our restaurants. A decline in traffic at these locations for a sustained period could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations (collectively, "our Results").

Opening and profitably operating new restaurants in existing and new markets is key to our growth. We remain focused on disciplined growth and development, building new restaurants designed for strong unit economics, attractive four-wall returns, and efficient capital deployment that will fuel long-term growth. As part of that process, we may struggle to identify target markets, we may not be able to open our planned new restaurants within budget or on a timely basis, and our new restaurants may not perform as well as anticipated. New restaurant success is affected by several factors, many of which are beyond our control, including our ability to secure a sufficient pipeline of appropriate and attractive sites, and to complete construction in a timely and cost-efficient manner.

In fiscal 2025, we continued to make progress against our long-term strategic priorities while managing significant operational and leadership transitions. As further discussed in Part I, Item 1. Business, we launched our loyalty program, Portillo's Perks™ ("Perks"), and opened eight new restaurants, including our first location in Georgia and our first in-line restaurant.

In September 2025, the Company announced a strategic reset to its development strategy, following disappointing results from new market expansion, particularly in Texas. Going forward, we plan to enter new markets more gradually, tapping into the pent up demand from Portillo's fans across the country, but recognizing that it takes time to build awareness and adoption among consumers who are not yet familiar with the brand. Instead of rapidly building out markets, as we did in Dallas-Ft. Worth and Houston, we will take a more measured approach with new restaurants separated by more time and distance. We have implemented this roadmap to our entry into the Atlanta, Georgia market. The first Portillo's opened in Kennesaw, Georgia in November of 2025 and the next restaurant will not open until 2027.

We also continue to refine our prototype to improve the unit economics while also maximizing the guest and team member experience. In 2025, with the exception of one in-line restaurant and one Portillo's pickup restaurant, all new restaurant openings were our Restaurant of the Future ("RoTF 1.0") design, a 6,250 square foot restaurant. All of the free standing restaurants scheduled to open in 2026 will follow that prototype. In 2027, we plan to debut our Restaurant of the Future 2.0 design.

In fiscal 2025, total revenue grew 3.0%, primarily due to new restaurant openings in 2025 and 2024. Same-restaurant sales declined 0.5% during fiscal 2025, compared to a decline of 0.6% during fiscal 2024.

Commodity inflation was 3.9% in fiscal 2025 compared to 4.2% in fiscal 2024. In fiscal 2025, we experienced an increase of 0.7% in labor expenses, as a percentage of revenue, compared to fiscal 2024 primarily due to lower transactions, incremental wage rate increases, deleverage from our newer restaurant openings, and higher benefit costs, partially offset by labor efficiencies and a higher average check.

In 2026, we will focus on executing strategies that strengthen transaction growth across our restaurants while optimizing returns on our new restaurants. We will leverage our Perks platform to drive trial and frequency, prioritize operational excellence, and invest in our team members. These priorities support our commitment to positive free cash flow and delivering long-term value.

paragraphs: Portillo's Inc. (the "Company") 於 2021 年 6 月 8 日在特拉華州成立為一家公司，目的是為了促進首次公開發行 ("IPO") 以及其他相關交易，以進行 PHD Group Holdings LLC 及其子公司 ("Portillo's OpCo") 的業務。本公司成為 Portillo's OpCo 唯一的管理成員，並經營及控制 Portillo's OpCo 的所有業務與事務。因此，本公司將 Portillo's OpCo 的財務結果合併，並報告非控制性權益，代表其他成員 ("pre-IPO LLC Members") 在 Portillo's OpCo 所持有的經濟權益。Portillo's Inc. 的 A 級普通股於納斯達克交易，代碼為 "PTLO"。除非文意另有明確說明，否則文中 "we," "us," "our," "Portillo's," "the Company" 及其他類似詞彙均指 Portillo's Inc. 及其子公司，包括 Portillo's OpCo。

截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日財務年度 ("fiscal 2025")，我們經營 102 家餐廳，分佈於 11 個州，包括由 C&O Chicago, L.L.C. ("C&O") 所擁有的一家餐廳，我們持有其中 50% 的權益。截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，本公司持有 Portillo's OpCo 的 95.4%，而 pre-IPO LLC Members 持有其餘 4.6% 的 Portillo's OpCo。
本公司與其他方簽訂聯營協議，以發展及營運位於達拉斯-沃斯堡國際機場 ("DFW") 的餐廳
預計於 2026 年開始營運。本公司持有 AP Dogs, LLC ("AP Dogs") 65% 的權益，並擁有該公司的日常營運控制權。
本公司對其業務及事務擁有實際的經營與管理控制權。因此，本公司將合併該合資企業，並報告其
非控制性權益，代表其他夥伴持有的AP Dogs經濟權益。

Portillo's提供芝加哥經典街頭美食，在高能量、多通路的餐廳中，設計用以激發感官並創造難忘的用餐體驗。自1963年Dick Portillo在一個他稱為『The Dog House』的小 trailers 裡創立以來，我們已成長為一個受愛戴的品牌，擁有熱情（有人可能說是癲狂）的全國性追隨者。我們多樣化的菜單包含所有美國經典美食，例如芝加哥風格熱狗與香腸、義大利牛肉三明治、炭烤漢堡、新鮮切碎沙拉、捲脆薯條、自制巧克力蛋糕以及我們的招牌巧克力蛋糕奶昔。我們透過結合快速餐飲（"QSR"）概念的最佳特點與充滿活力的氛圍，創造獨一無二的消費者體驗，並在能產生龐大銷售量的餐廳模式中運作。我們幾乎所有的餐廳均設有雙車道 drive-thru，並經過精心設計，以適應多種進場方式，包括內用、外帶、外送及婚宴服務，以迅速且高效地服務顧客。我們相信，我們令人垂涎的食物、多通路銷售模式、對運營卓越的承諾，以及獨特的員工驅動文化，使我們擁有競爭優勢。我們的業務，包括許多下列所述的要素，受到某些風險影響，這些風險可能對我們實現理想結果的能力造成重大且不利的影響。如需更深入討論這些風險，請參閱第一部分，第1A項，"風險因素"。
一個受愛戴的經典品牌，擁有癲狂且終身的忠實粉絲。我們透過每一餐的服務，打動顧客的心、思想與胃。我們的菜單為所有人提供選擇，吸引廣泛的客羣，使我們的餐廳能蓬勃發展，並在多個用餐時段、平日及場閤中產生強而平衡的銷售量。
活潑的餐廳氛圍能吸引顧客的感官體驗。雖然我們的營運模式著重於快速將美味、現點現做的食物送到顧客手中，我們認為我們的氛圍讓用餐體驗不僅僅是一頓美味的餐點。當顧客走進 Portillo's 時，他們會沉浸在一種與其他連鎖餐廳完全不同的體驗中。我們的餐廳透過活潑、放鬆且難忘的氛圍，來激發所有感官。

我們的用餐區營造出懷舊與地方特色。每間餐廳都有其獨特的主題裝潢，從 1930 年代禁酒令風格，到 1950 年代速食店風格，再到 1960 年代花漾巴士風格，以及復古汽車工坊風格。音樂也與主題相呼應，從 ragtime 到 doo wop 到 disco。每個細節都不馬虎，無論是燈光、招牌，甚至是天花板上若隱若現的星星。每間餐廳也從當地社區汲取設計元素。空間規劃讓個人用餐者、家庭、大型團體，甚至婚禮賓客都能感到舒適。

除了空間本身，我們認為 Portillo's 的氣氛是獨一無二的。顧客可以看見我們開放式的廚房，餐點就在他們眼前準備。漢堡煎烤、薯條油炸、牛肉在肉汁中燉煮的香味從廚房傳來。每道完成的餐點都會搭配一個有趣的口令（"Number two, we got you!"; "Number seven, welcome to Portillo's heaven!")。但最重要的是，這份氣氛來自於眾多顧客的熱情，他們都興奮地在這裡享受 Portillo's 的體驗。我們希望每位造訪的顧客都能帶著美好的回憶、滿足的胃口，以及想要再次來的渴望。

維護我們親愛品牌的本質。Portillo's 希望在傳統銷售通路提供業界領先的體驗，同時持續在成長型銷售通路進行創新與擴張。親臨現場用餐能提供最佳的 Portillo's 用餐體驗，因此我們努力讓親臨現場的體驗體現 Portillo's 的核心價值：家庭、卓越、活力與樂趣。在 drive-thru 通路，我們致力於在速度、服務與準確度方面保持業界領先。在數位取餐、外送與餐飲服務等銷售通路，我們在運營上已取得顯著進展，這將有助於我們爭取更多的市場份額。
Portillo's 自 1980 年代起就開創了 drive-thru 模式，結合速度與服務，透過外場點餐員、餐點遞送員與多車道 drive-thru 設施。我們的團隊持續致力於改善與創新 drive-thru 服務，以提升服務效率與訂單準確度。新開設的餐廳都會設有 drive-thru 門口，以協助遞送員並提升顧客體驗。
體驗、服務與餐點品質定義了我們品牌的價值，但維持具競爭力的價格仍是我們在餐飲業廣泛競爭中極為重要的考量。我們持續監測許多與顧客相關的餐點類別與場合的價格點。為了未來的成功，我們會持續執行價格策略，並著重於運營卓越，目標是與速食餐廳競爭者相比，維持無可比擬的價值。

* 調整後 EBITDA 及 餐廳層級調整後 EBITDA 為非 GAAP 財務指標。調整後 EBITDA 與淨利（損）及 餐廳層級調整後 EBITDA 與營運獲利，最直接可比的財務指標，依 GAAP 會計準則所呈現，詳見 "關鍵績效指標及非 GAAP 財務指標" 章節。
在 2025 財年，我們持續在長遠戰略優先事項上取得進展，同時管理重大的營運與領導層轉變。如進一步討論於第一部分，項目 1. 事業，我們啟動了忠誠度計畫，Portillo's Perks™（"Perks"），並開設了八家新餐廳，包括我們在喬治亞州的第一家門店及第一家內線餐廳。

2025 年 9 月，本公司宣佈對其發展策略進行戰略重設，因新市場擴張的結果令人失望，特別是在德克薩斯州。展望未來，我們計畫以較為緩慢的方式進入新市場，利用 Portillo's 粉絲全國範圍內的潛在需求，但也認知到，要建立消費者對品牌的認知與接受度需要時間。我們不會像在達拉斯-沃斯堡與休士頓那樣快速擴張市場，而是會以更謹慎的方式，以較長的時間與距離來分開開設新餐廳。我們已實施此進入亞特蘭大、喬治亞州市場的路線圖。第一家 Portillo's 於 2025 年 11 月在喬治亞州肯納索開設，下一家餐廳將於 2027 年才開設。
我們也持續優化原型設計，以改善單店經濟效益，同時最大化顧客與員工的體驗。在 2025 年，除了一家內線餐廳與一家 Portillo's 取餐餐廳外，所有新開設的餐廳皆為我們的未來餐廳（"RoTF 1.0"）設計，為 6,250 平方英尺的餐廳。所有預計於 2026 年開設的獨立餐廳皆將遵循此原型。在 2027 年，我們計畫推出我們的未來餐廳 2.0 設計。
在 2025 財年，總營業收入成長 3.0%，主要因 2025 年及 2024 年新餐廳開設。同店銷售額在 2025 財年減少 0.5%，與 2024 財年減少 0.6% 相較。
通貨膨脹率在會計年度 2025 年為 3.9%，較會計年度 2024 年的 4.2% 降低。在會計年度 2025 年，我們的勞動費用佔營業收入百分比上升了 0.7%，與會計年度 2024 年相比，主要由於交易量減少、累積工資率上漲、新開餐廳的去槓桿化以及更高的福利成本，部分抵銷了勞動效率提升及平均消費金額提高的影響。
在 2026 年，我們將專注於執行強化餐廳交易成長的策略，同時優化新開餐廳的回報。我們將運用 Perks 平台來推動試用率與消費頻率，優先追求運營卓越，並投資於我們的團隊成員。這些優先事項支持我們對正向自由現金流及長期價值創造的承諾。

headings: 與本公司業務、產業及成長策略相關之風險
本公司易受總體經濟條件變動、食品及原物料成本上漲及消費者偏好改變之影響。
本公司可能無法開設新餐廳或建立新市場，或新開設之餐廳表現不如預期，無法獲利，或最終關閉。
本公司之成長計畫及持續資本支出（"capex"）需求，需投入資金，而資金可能無法即時取得。
本公司同店銷售額未來期間可能低於預期。
食品安全問題及食物中毒事件可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司面對大量顧客競爭，若無法有效競爭，可能影響人流量、銷售額及營運毛利，進而對本公司營運成果產生重大不利影響。
本公司餐廳主要集中於美國中西部地區，若該地區出現特殊狀況，可能對本公司產生負面影響。
對本公司聲譽的損害及負面宣傳可能對本公司結果產生重大不利影響。
數位及配送業務及其擴張存在不確定性，並伴隨內在風險。
若本公司兩間酒廠運作持續中斷，可能對本公司業務造成損害。
若本公司在成長過程中無法維持企業文化，可能對本公司業務產生重大不利影響。
與僱用及勞動法相關的事項可能對本公司產生重大不利影響，導致訴訟或工會活動，增加重大成本並分散管理層注意力。
勞動品質、勞動力短缺或勞動成本增加可能對本公司結果產生重大不利影響。
本公司面臨與租賃不動產相關的風險，包括長期不可取消租約及無法續約到期租約的潛在可能性。
本公司業務面臨與銷售酒精飲料相關的風險。
本公司 goodwill、無限期壽命無形資產或長壽命資產之攤銷價值減損，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
天然災害、異常天氣條件、疫情爆發、政治事件、戰爭及恐怖主義等，可能幹擾本公司業務，導致銷售減少、營運成本及資本支出增加。
對環境永續及社會倡議的重視，可能增加本公司成本、損害本公司聲譽，並對本公司結果造成不利影響。
本公司在災難或不可抗力事件後，無法或失敗執行完整的業務持續性計畫，可能對本公司結果造成重大不利影響。
與本公司負債相關之風險
本公司負債水平可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響，並限制本公司規劃或應對業務變動之能力。
與本公司組織結構相關之風險
在某些情況下，Portillo's OpCo 需要向本公司及其他 LLC Units 持有人進行分紅，且該分紅可能相當重大。
本公司之組織架構，包括稅收應收協議（"TRA"），使本公司之業務產生複雜性。
與智慧財產權、資訊科技及資料安全相關之風險
未能保護及維護本公司之智慧財產權，包括本公司之商標，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
paragraphs: 您應仔細審閱下列風險因素，並與本年度10-K形式年度報告及其他公開揭露資訊一併考量。我們的業務面臨許多風險，包括可能使我們無法達成業務目標，或對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流、流動性或取得資金來源造成不利影響的風險，以及可能影響本公司A類普通股市場價值的風險。這些風險可能導致我們未來的結果與歷史結果，或我們對未來財務表現的預期有重大差異。下列所描述的風險突顯了可能對我們業務造成不利影響的潛在事件、趨勢或其他情況。
如同其他餐飲業公司，我們依賴食品與原物料的可得性，其成本會影響我們的業務與結果。食品與原物料的成本與可得性可能波動，並受許多我們無法控制的因素影響，包括總體經濟狀況、通貨膨脹、人力短缺、季節性波動、天氣與氣候條件、能源成本、全球需求、貿易保護與補貼、食品安全問題、傳染性疾病、可能的恐怖攻擊、網路攻擊、運輸問題、貨幣波動、產品回收，以及政府規範等。
過去食品與原物料成本的波動已影響我們的獲利與聲譽，未來也可能如此。雖然部分原物料受合約價格規範，但當合約到期時，我們可能無法成功重新協議條款以保護我們免受通貨膨脹影響，或未受合約價格規範的部分可能意外增加，造成未預期的價格通脹。我們在2025年12月28日結業年度及2024年12月29日結業年度，分別經歷了3.9%與4.2%的原物料價格通脹。

若我們的原料成本增加，我們可能暫停或永久停售某些餐點，而非支付較高的原料成本。這些對我們餐點的變動可能在短缺期間及之後，對我們的餐廳人潮與營運結果造成負面影響。此外，我們可能無法完全或部分抵銷未來成本增加，透過餐點價格上漲。競爭情況可能限制我們的餐點價格調整彈性，而實施餐點價格上漲可能改變顧客的造訪頻率或購買新模式。我們的產業依賴消費者可支配支出，並受消費品味改變及總體與微觀經濟條件（包括經濟衰退、消費者情緒、通貨膨脹或食品或能源成本增加）的影響。例如人潮模式、天氣、燃料價格、地方人口結構、地方規範及競爭環境等因素，可能對我們各個據點的表現造成不利影響。
我們的餐廳主要位於高人潮活動商圈，這些商圈通常包含零售、生活方式及娛樂中心。我們依賴這些商圈的高訪客人數來吸引顧客造訪我們的餐廳。若這些據點的訪客人數持續下降，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果（統稱為「我們的營運結果」）造成重大不利影響。

在現有及新市場開設並成功營運新餐廳，是我們成長的關鍵。我們持續專注於嚴謹的成長與發展，建造設計良好的新餐廳，以實現強勁的單店經濟效益、吸引人的四壁回報率及高效的資金運用，以推動長期成長。在這個過程中，我們可能難以識別目標市場，可能無法在預算內或按時開設我們計畫中的新餐廳，且新開設的餐廳可能表現不如預期。新餐廳的成功受多種因素影響，許多因素超出我們的控制範圍，包括我們能否取得足夠且合適且有吸引力的場地，以及能否在時間與成本效益上完成建設。
